1: # Issue tracker
2: 
3: Issues are tracked in **Linear** using the `linctl` CLI.
4: 
5: ## Workflow
6: 
7: Use `linctl` for issue operations in this repo. Do not use GitHub Issues or local `.scratch/` markdown issues unless the repo configuration changes.
8: 
9: Issue identifiers follow the format `DHC-123`.
10: 
11: Use the Linear CLI to create an issue with the appropriate team/project, title, description, and triage label/status.
12: 
13: ```bash
14: linctl issue create --title "Title" --description "Body"
15: ```
16: 
17: ## CLI usage
18: 
19: ```bash
20: linctl issue list
21: ```
22: 
23: ## Viewing an issue
24: 
25: ```bash
26: linctl issue get <issue-id>
27: ```
28: 
29: This installed `linctl` does not provide `issue view`; use `issue get` for issue details.
30: 
31: ## Updating triage state
32: 
33: Apply the matching triage label/status string from `docs/agents/triage-labels.md` using `linctl`.
34: 
35: Repository: `alessandrojcm/dhc-dashboard`
36: 
37: ## Projects & milestones
38: 
39: - Feature tickets may target the `DHC Dashboard` project: `linctl issue create --team ALE --project "DHC Dashboard" ...`, optionally with `--project-milestone <name>` for release grouping (e.g. `v3`).
40: - linctl has no milestone management subcommand. Create milestones via raw GraphQL:
41:   `linctl graphql -q 'mutation { projectMilestoneCreate(input: { projectId: "<project-uuid>", name: "<name>" }) { success projectMilestone { id name } } }'`
42:   Get the project UUID from `linctl project list -j` / `linctl project get`.
43: 
44: ## Wayfinding operations
45: 
46: - Wayfinder maps use `wayfinder:map`; child tickets use exactly one of `wayfinder:research`, `wayfinder:prototype`, `wayfinder:grilling`, or `wayfinder:task`.
47: - Create all map tickets first, then attach each child with `linctl issue update <child> --parent <map>`.
48: - Express blocking with Linear relations: `linctl issue relation add <blocker> --blocks <blocked>`.
49: - The frontier is the map's open, unassigned children whose blocking relations are all closed. Claim one before work with `linctl issue assign <ticket>`.
50: - Verify the map and its children with `linctl issue get <map>`, and inspect dependency edges with `linctl issue relation list <ticket>`.
51: 
52: ## Relation direction gotcha
53: 
54: Agents keep entering `--blocks` relations backwards. The flag points **from the blocker toward the blocked issue**: `linctl issue relation add ALE-A --blocks ALE-B` means **ALE-A must finish before ALE-B** (ALE-A is the prerequisite, ALE-B is the dependent). Equivalently, read it as "ALE-A blocks ALE-B."
55: 
56: When sequencing an expand→code→contract split (e.g. ALE-179), the correct edges are: expand `--blocks` code, and code `--blocks` contract. The expand migration is the frontier, not the contract. Before treating a Linear-reported "unblocked" issue as the frontier, cross-check it against the spec's stated ordering — if Linear's graph disagrees with the spec, the relations are inverted and must be fixed (`relation remove` the wrong edge, then `relation add` the correct one) before claiming the ticket.

(End of file - total 56 lines)
</content>

1: # Commands
2: 
3: All tasks are defined in `.mise.toml`. Run `mise tasks` to list them all.
4: 
5: ## Setup
6: 
7: ```bash
8: # First time: install all pinned tools (Node, Erlang, Elixir, pnpm)
9: mise install
10: 
11: # Activate mise in your shell (one-time, add to your shell rc)
12: eval "$(mise activate bash)"    # bash
13: eval "$(mise activate zsh)"     # zsh
14: mise activate fish | source     # fish
15: ```
16: 
17: After activation, `node`, `elixir`, `mix`, `pnpm` etc. resolve to the versions pinned in `.mise.toml` on every `cd`.
18: 
19: ## SvelteKit (`apps/web`)
20: 
21: ```bash
22: # Dev (start in order)
23: docker compose up -d db mailpit   # 1. Start PostgreSQL + Mailpit (dev email catcher)
24: mise run phx-server               # 2. Phoenix API and Oban workers
25: mise run dev                      # 3. SvelteKit dev from apps/web
26: ```
27: 
28: - The SvelteKit dev server serves **HTTPS** at the canonical local origin `https://127.0.0.1:5173` (`vite-plugin-mkcert`, self-signed). Probe it with `curl -sk https://127.0.0.1:5173/...`; plain `http://` curls fail even when the server is up. Keep frontend URLs, redirects, and browser visits on `127.0.0.1` rather than mixing it with `localhost`, because host-only auth cookies do not cross between them.
29: - Phoenix remains on `http://127.0.0.1:4000` in development. Since the browser frontend and API use different schemes, development auth cookies are intentionally `Secure; SameSite=None` and browser API calls use credentialed CORS. E2E remains a separate HTTP-only `127.0.0.1` topology with `SameSite=Lax` cookies.
30: - Unhandled server errors are console-logged (status, method, path, route, stack) by `logUnhandledServerError` in `apps/web/src/hooks.server.ts`, wrapped inside Sentry's `handleError`. The catch-all UI is the root `apps/web/src/routes/+error.svelte` plus `apps/web/src/error.html` (fallback for errors in `handle`, `+server.js`, or the root layout load, which no `+error.svelte` can render).
31: 
32: ```bash
33: 
34: # Testing
35: mise run test-unit          # Vitest
36: mise run test-browser       # Vitest Browser Mode component tests in Chromium
37: STRIPE_SECRET_KEY=sk_test_... mise run test-e2e
38:                             # Playwright + real Stripe test mode; self-starts disposable PostgreSQL, Phoenix, and SvelteKit
39: mise run check              # Svelte type check (NOT raw tsc)
40: 
41: # Lint & format
42: mise run lint               # Oxlint (web Svelte/JS/TS + API client TS)
43: mise run format             # Auto-format with Oxfmt
44: ```
45: 
46: Oxlint runs in `apps/web`, `packages/api-client`, and `packages/email-templates`;
47: the generated API client under `packages/api-client/src/client/` is ignored.
48: Oxfmt covers `apps/web` and `packages/email-templates`.
49: The shared config loads the project-local anti-slop plugin from
50: `tools/oxlint/anti-slop/`; keep `oxlint` and `@oxlint/plugins` on the same pinned
51: version when upgrading it, and leave all anti-slop rules enabled at error severity.
52: 
53: Playwright starts its Phoenix and SvelteKit processes through the internal
54: `e2e-phoenix-server` and `e2e-web-server` mise tasks. Their task-local environment
55: is the source of truth for E2E server settings; do not duplicate those variables
56: in `playwright.config.ts` command strings.
57: 
58: ## Dev email catching (Mailpit)
59: 
60: The compose file ships a `mailpit` service (`axllent/mailpit`). In dev, the
61: email worker (`Dhc.Email.Worker`) delivers through Swoosh's Mailpit **HTTP**
62: adapter (ADR 0021): each job arrives as a real message whose body is the
63: pretty-printed JSON summary (recipient, friendly template name, data
64: variables), since only the provider can render the real templates. Web UI at
65: `http://localhost:8025` (override with `MAILPIT_HTTP_URL`; the SMTP port 1025
66: is no longer used). Messages are in-memory and lost on container restart. A
67: stopped Mailpit container is not an error: delivery failures log a warning and
68: the job still succeeds.
69: 
70: The E2E suite intentionally uses Stripe's real test API for invitation acceptance.
71: It fails before startup unless `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY` starts with `sk_test_`. The test
72: account must provide active `monthly_membership_fee` and `annual_membership_fee`
73: lookup-key prices; coupon tests create unique promotion fixtures and clean them up.
74: Never supply a live-mode key.
75: 
76: ## Email templates (Resend sync)
77: 
78: The five transactional templates are React Email components in
79: `packages/email-templates`, synced upsert-by-alias to Resend-hosted templates
80: (ADR 0022). See that package's README for the drift policy and CI wiring.
81: 
82: ```bash
83: mise run email-sync          # render + upsert drafts (what PRs do)
84: mise run email-sync-publish  # upsert + publish (what merge-to-main does)
85: mise run email-smoke         # fail unless every whitelisted kind has a published template
86: ```
87: 
88: All three need a Full Access key as `RESEND_API_KEY` (`fnox` holds the send-only
89: key under that name; use the `RESEND_API_KEY_CI` value for syncs). The GitHub
90: Actions workflow `.github/workflows/email-templates.yml` runs the same pipeline:
91: drafts on pull requests, publish + smoke on main, gated by change detection on
92: `packages/email-templates/**`.
93: 
94: Template assets (the crest) are served from the R2 bucket `dhc-email-assets`
95: at `https://assets.dublinhemaclub.com`, decoupled from the web app. After
96: changing files in `packages/email-templates/emails/static/`, run
97: `mise run email-asset-upload` (needs `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN` or an interactive
98: `wrangler login`; one-time bootstrap: create the bucket and attach its custom
99: domain).
100: 
101: ## Phoenix (in progress)
102: 
103: Phoenix mise tasks override the root Supabase Docker `.env` database host and connect to host-local Supabase Postgres at `localhost:54322`.
104: 
105: ```bash
106: # Setup (first time)
107: mise run phx-setup          # deps.get + ecto.create + ecto.migrate
108: 
109: # Server
110: mise run phx-server         # Start dev server (hot-reload) on :4000
111: mise run phx-console        # Start server inside IEx interactive shell
112: 
113: # Database
114: mise run phx-migrate        # Run pending migrations
115: mise run phx-rollback       # Rollback last migration
116: mise run phx-gen-migration NAME  # Generate a new migration
117: ```
118: 
119: ### One-off Discord roster export and assignment review
120: 
121: Export the existing guild roster once with `@discordjs/rest`, which handles
122: Discord rate limits while the script paginates through the guild. The bot token
123: and guild ID come only from the process environment. The script writes
124: `roster.json` with mode `0600`; keep it restricted and delete it after the
125: migration review window.
126: 
127: ```bash
128: DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN=... \
129: DISCORD_GUILD_ID=... \
130: node scripts/discord-roster-export.mjs
131: 
132: # Stage rows are a plain JSON array of
133: # {"principal_id":"...","discord_user_id":"...","username_snapshot":"..."}.
134: # The command prints the generated capture ID used by the later phases.
135: cd apps/phoenix
136: DISCORD_SUBJECT_FINGERPRINT_KEY=... \
137: mix dhc.discord.assignments stage ../../roster.json /secure/path/stage-rows.json PREPARER_PRINCIPAL_ID
138: 
139: # Review displays the selected roster evidence. Apply-review consumes a plain
140: # array of {"assignment_id":"...","decision":"approve|reject"}.
141: mix dhc.discord.assignments review CAPTURE_ID ../../roster.json REVIEWER_PRINCIPAL_ID
142: DISCORD_SUBJECT_FINGERPRINT_KEY=... \
143: mix dhc.discord.assignments apply-review CAPTURE_ID /secure/path/review-rows.json REVIEWER_PRINCIPAL_ID
144: 
145: DISCORD_SUBJECT_FINGERPRINT_KEY=... \
146: mix dhc.discord.assignments report CAPTURE_ID ../../roster.json
147: ```
148: 
149: The separately authenticated operator supplies the preparer and reviewer IDs;
150: the task authorizes both against current Member-admin roles in the database, and
151: they must be different. The ID arguments are not authentication credentials.
152: The roster exporter is throwaway migration tooling, not a recurring sync or
153: Phoenix runtime task.
154: 
155: # Code quality
156: mise run phx-format         # Format all Elixir files
157: mise run phx-format-check   # Check formatting (CI)
158: mise run phx-reach          # Reach architecture policy checks (.reach.exs)
159: mise run phx-precommit      # Full check: credo + reach arch + audit + compile + unlock + format + test
160: 
161: # Testing
162: mise run phx-test           # Run all Phoenix tests (excludes :integration tests)
163: 
164: # For specific test files, run directly:
165: cd apps/phoenix && mix test test/some_test.exs
166: cd apps/phoenix && mix test --failed     # Re-run only failed tests
167: cd apps/phoenix && mix ecto.migrations   # Show migration status
168: 
169: # Integration tests are excluded by default. Run with:
170: cd apps/phoenix && mix test --include integration
171: cd apps/phoenix && mix test test/dhc/stripe_sync/workers/worker_integration_test.exs --include integration
172: 
173: # Stripe sync integration test hits Stripe test mode and creates its own
174: # customers/subscriptions. Required: STRIPE_SECRET_KEY. STRIPE_SYNC_TEST_PRICE_ID
175: # is optional when lookup_key=standard_membership_fee exists in Stripe test mode.
176: cd apps/phoenix && \
177:   STRIPE_SECRET_KEY=sk_test_... \
178:   STRIPE_SYNC_TEST_PRICE_ID=price_... \
179:   mix test test/dhc/stripe_sync/workers/worker_integration_test.exs --include integration
180: ```
181: 
182: Tests that use `Ecto.Adapters.SQL.Sandbox.unboxed_run/2` commit outside the
183: per-test sandbox transaction and must explicitly delete every durable fixture
184: in `on_exit/1`. If teardown must remove immutable Discord assignment audit rows,
185: disable only `discord_assignment_reject_audit_mutation` for that deletion and
186: always re-enable it in an `after` block.
187: 
188: ### Reach architecture policy (`apps/phoenix/.reach.exs`)
189: 
190: Reach (`mix reach.check --arch`, also in the `precommit` alias) enforces module-boundary rules Credo cannot express:
191: 
192: - Layers: `DhcWeb.*` / `Dhc.*` / `Dhc.Repo`; domain must not depend on web (except `DhcWeb.Endpoint` infrastructure edges), Repo must not depend on web, and the web layer must not touch the Repo directly (`DhcWeb.Plugs.MagicLinkRateLimit` is the one documented seam).
193: - Forbidden calls: `Dhc.Stripe.Client.request/1` outside the client itself (Stripe goes through generated `Dhc.Stripe.Operations.*`), any `Nostrum.*` outside `Dhc.Discord.*`, `HTTPoison`/`Tesla`/`:httpc` anywhere, and `IO.puts` outside Mix tasks and `Dhc.Release`.
194: 
195: Findings are fingerprinted against `.reach-baseline.json`. New findings fail the build; only baseline a known transitional finding with:
196: 
197: ```bash
198: cd apps/phoenix && MIX_ENV=dev mix reach.check --arch --write-baseline .reach-baseline.json
199: ```
200: 
201: The config pins `checks.source_paths: ["lib"]`, so one baseline stays valid across dev and test environments.
202: 
203: ### Sentry (production error tracking)
204: 
205: Sentry activates automatically when `SENTRY_DSN` env var is set. Inactive otherwise.
206: 
207: ```bash
208: # Enable Sentry (set this in production)
209: export SENTRY_DSN="https://your-dsn@sentry.io/your-project-id"
210: ```
211: 
212: Sentry captures:
213: - Unhandled exceptions in HTTP requests (via `Sentry.PlugContext`)
214: - Failed Oban jobs (via Oban integration)
215: - `Logger.error/1` calls and process crashes (via `Sentry.LoggerHandler`)
216: - Oban cron check-ins (optional, for cron monitoring)
217: 
218: ### Fly.io deployment (Phoenix API)
219: 
220: Phoenix deploys to Fly.io as an Elixir release built by `apps/phoenix/Dockerfile`, with `fly.toml` at the repo root.
221: 
222: ```bash
223: # Required locally/CI: flyctl and FLY_API_TOKEN
224: mise run phx-fly-deploy        # fly deploy --depot (Fly Depot builder, persistent org-scoped layer cache)
225: ```
226: 
227: The container runs Phoenix through `fnox exec --profile production -- /app/bin/dhc start`, and the Fly release command runs migrations through the same fnox profile. `fnox.toml` uses the `production` profile and 1Password vault `Production-phoenix-api`. Create one 1Password item per runtime env var (for example `DATABASE_URL`, `SECRET_KEY_BASE`, `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY`) with the value in the item's password field.
228: 
229: The only runtime bootstrap secret stored in Fly should be `OP_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_TOKEN`, scoped to the 1Password production vault:
230: 
231: ```bash
232: fly secrets set OP_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_TOKEN=ops_... --app dhc-dashboard
233: ```
234: 
235: Rotating app secrets in 1Password does not require `fly secrets set` or a new image; restart Machines to reload them through `fnox exec`. Only rotate the Fly secret when the 1Password service account token itself changes.
236: 
237: GitHub Actions workflow: `.github/workflows/deploy-phoenix-fly.yml`. Required GitHub secret: `FLY_API_TOKEN`. Optional GitHub variable: `FLY_PHOENIX_APP` (defaults to `dhc-dashboard`).
238: 
239: The workflow builds with `flyctl deploy --depot` (Fly's Depot builder), which provides persistent org-scoped Docker layer caching across builds. This is faster and more deterministic than `--remote-only`'s pooled builder, which may hand you a cold VM with no cache. The mise toolchain is installed inside the Dockerfile during the remote build, so the workflow does not install mise on the GitHub runner.
240: 
241: ## API Contract (full pipeline)
242: 
243: Regenerate **both** sides of the API contract — Phoenix controller stubs and TypeScript client — in one step:
244: 
245: ```bash
246: mise run api-gen
247: ```
248: 
249: Fails fast: if either step exits non-zero, mise stops immediately and does not proceed.
250: 
251: **`mix gen.controllers` clobber caveat**: the task maps every operation under a tag to a REST action derived from HTTP method + path (or `operationId`), and regenerates the *whole* controller + JSON renderer + contract test for that tag. When a tag carries multiple non-REST operations (e.g. `Members` has `members.list`, `members.analytics`, `members.insuranceForm`), `--force=<path>` will overwrite the controller with stubs that map *all three* to `index` and call a non-existent `Members.list_members()` — clobbering any hand-written action bodies. After regenerating, restore the hand-written controller (keep your real action names + bodies) and never re-run `--force` on a tag whose controller you've fleshed out unless you're prepared to restore it from git. The JSON renderer and contract test are likewise tag-scoped, so extend them by hand for non-REST operations.
252: 
253: ## API Client (TypeScript)
254: 
255: ```bash
256: # Generate client from OpenAPI spec (from project root)
257: mise run api-gen
258: 
259: # Or run just the TS side
260: pnpm api-gen
261: 
262: # Watch mode (regenerate on spec changes)
263: pnpm --filter @dhc/api-client api:generate:watch
264: ```
265: 
266: Generated output: `packages/api-client/src/client/` (gitignored — auto-regenerated on `pnpm install` via postinstall, do not manually edit)
267: 
268: **Manual step after `mise run api-gen`**: `packages/api-client/src/index.ts` is hand-maintained (tracked, not generated). `openapi-ts` only writes to `src/client/`; it does not update the public re-exports in `src/index.ts`. After adding a new operation, manually add the generated SDK function plus its `types.gen` / `valibot.gen` / `@tanstack/svelte-query.gen` exports to the four `export` blocks in `src/index.ts` (mirror how `waitlistStatus` / `membersInsuranceForm` are exposed). Without this, the function exists in `src/client/` but is not importable from `@dhc/api-client`.
269: 
270: `packages/api-client/openapi-ts.config.ts` explicitly points `output.tsConfigPath` at `packages/api-client/tsconfig.json` so postinstall generation works in deployment environments that do not expose the repo-root SvelteKit `tsconfig.json`.
271: 
272: `@hey-api/openapi-ts` + Valibot currently emits invalid TypeScript for boolean schemas expressed as `enum: [true]`/`enum: [false]` (it generates `v.picklist([true])`, but Valibot picklists are typed for string/number/bigint). For response flags that are always true on success, use `type: boolean` plus a description instead of a single-value boolean enum.
273: 
274: Usage in SvelteKit:
275: ```ts
276: import { configureClient, healthIndex } from '@dhc/api-client';
277: 
278: // Configure once at app startup (e.g., +layout.svelte or hooks)
279: configureClient({
280:   baseUrl: 'http://localhost:4000/api',
281:   getAuthToken: async () => {
282:     const { data } = await supabase.auth.getSession();
283:     return data.session?.access_token;
284:   },
285: });
286: 
287: // Then use SDK functions
288: const { data, error } = await healthIndex();
289: ```
290: 
291: ## Stripe API Client (Elixir, generated)
292: 
293: ```bash
294: # Regenerate from Stripe OpenAPI spec (downloads spec, trims, generates)
295: mise run stripe-gen
296: ```
297: 
298: Generated output: `apps/phoenix/lib/dhc/stripe/generated/` (committed so production builds do not need to regenerate it; do not manually edit).
299: 
300: To add new Stripe endpoints:
301: 1. Add the operation ID to `@allowed_operations` in `apps/phoenix/lib/mix/tasks/stripe.gen.ex`
302: 2. Also add it to `@allowed_operations` in `apps/phoenix/dev/dhc/stripe/processor.ex` (the oapi_generator filter)
303: 3. Run `mise run stripe-gen` (or `cd apps/phoenix && MIX_ENV=dev mix stripe.gen`)
304: 4. Commit the regenerated output in `apps/phoenix/lib/dhc/stripe/generated/`
305: 5. Use the generated functions via `Dhc.Stripe.Operations.*` with `Dhc.Stripe.Client`
306: 
307: - Do not hand-roll Stripe endpoint calls with `Dhc.Stripe.Client.request/1` in domain code. If an endpoint exists in Stripe's OpenAPI spec, find the operation ID by the Stripe URL, add that exact ID to both allow-lists above, regenerate, and call the generated `Dhc.Stripe.Operations.*` function. If generation still fails after both allow-lists match the current spec, debug the generator/filter rather than bypassing it.
308: 
309: Hand-written modules: `Dhc.Stripe.Client` (Req adapter), `Dhc.Stripe.Processor` (allowlist filter), `Dhc.StripeSync` (sync business logic), `Dhc.StripeSync.Worker` (Oban worker).
310: 
311: The Stripe API version is pinned in app config (`:stripe_api_version`, default `"2025-10-29.clover"`) and sent as the `Stripe-Version` header on every request. This matches the version used by the existing Deno edge functions (`src/lib/server/stripe.ts`). When updating, change the config value in all three env configs (`config.exs`, `dev.exs`, `test.exs`, `runtime.exs`), update `src/lib/server/stripe.ts`, and re-run `mise run stripe-gen`.
312: 
313: ## Seeds
314: 
315: ```bash
316: # Phoenix Mix tasks replacing legacy scripts/seed*.js
317: mise run seed-waitlist
318: mise run seed-waitlist 50
319: mise run seed-invitations
320: mise run seed-invitations 50
321: mise run seed-members
322: mise run seed-members 25
323: mise run seed-committee
324: mise run seed-committee ./scripts/users.csv
325: 
326: # Or run directly from Phoenix app
327: cd apps/phoenix && mix seed.waitlist 50
328: cd apps/phoenix && mix seed.invitations 50
329: cd apps/phoenix && mix seed.members 25
330: cd apps/phoenix && mix seed.committee_members ../../scripts/users.csv
331: ```
332: 
333: `mise` loads `.env` automatically; the seed Mix tasks do not load dotenv themselves. Keep `.env` up to date with the same Phoenix DB connection convention used by the app (`DATABASE_URL`, preferred). `seed.members`, `seed.workshops`, and `seed.committee_members` create Phoenix Principals directly through `Dhc.Auth`. `seed.invitations` creates direct, pending member invitations without a waitlist entry or an issuing administrator. `seed.members` only creates Stripe customers when `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY` is set. The committee CSV is intentionally local and gitignored because it contains member data; pass its path explicitly when `scripts/users.csv` is not present.
334: 
335: ## CI (full check)
336: 
337: ```bash
338: mise run ci                 # lint + format-check + type-check + unit tests
339: ```

1: # Code-Authored Templates Synced to Resend-Hosted Templates
2: 
3: **Status:** Accepted  
4: **Date:** 2026-08-22  
5: **Tags:** email, resend, react-email, templates, ci-cd
6: 
7: ## Context
8: 
9: Loops hosts transactional email templates in its dashboard: content and subject/sender metadata are invisible to the repository, unreviewable, and unauditable by agents. Migrating to Resend is the moment to flip template ownership. Resend offers two send models: dashboard-hosted templates (`template: {id, variables}`) or per-send inline `html`. Resend also supports authoring templates as React Email components and uploading them programmatically (official `resend` CLI; Templates API with stable aliases; draft→publish lifecycle with version history).
10: 
11: ## Decision
12: 
13: Each Email Kind is authored as a React Email component in a new `packages/email-templates` workspace package. The component file also declares its Template metadata — default subject, default sender, declared typed variables (`string | number`, optional fallback) — making TypeScript the single schema authority for what each Kind requires. The Elixir side keeps only its generic string|number validation; Resend enforces per-template variable contracts at send time.
14: 
15: Templates remain hosted at Resend. A sync pipeline renders components to HTML and uploads them via the official CLI/API:
16: 
17: - Pull requests upload drafts only; merging to main publishes. Publishing therefore gates on review plus required checks, never on an arbitrary push.
18: - Templates carry a stable alias derived mechanically from the Email Kind (kebab-case). Sends address `template.id` by that alias, so no kind→ID configuration map or env-var indirection exists at runtime.
19: - Dashboard edits to templates are drift; the next sync overwrites them. Resend's version history is the recovery mechanism.
20: 
21: The cutover from Loops is a single global adapter flip rehearsed against Resend's sandbox in dev (no staging environment exists), with Loops credentials kept warm for instant rollback.
22: 
23: ## Consequences
24: 
25: - Template changes deploy through git review like all other code; agents can read and write templates.
26: - The provider's template store remains part of the production path: a future provider migration must re-upload templates there. Accepted in exchange for hosted rendering, server-side variable interpolation/escaping, and zero rendering machinery in Elixir.
27: - Non-prod environments keep receiving a JSON summary of Kind + data variables in Mailpit rather than rendered HTML; visual previews happen through React Email's local preview server during authoring.
28: - A typo'd alias surfaces as a send-time validation error; mitigated by the compile-time Email Kind whitelist plus a check asserting every whitelisted Kind has a published template.
29: 
30: ## Considered options
31: 
32: - **Recreate templates in Resend's dashboard.** Rejected: closest to today's shape but keeps content invisible to the repo and would be throwaway work once code ownership landed.
33: - **App-shipped HTML** — render artifacts in-repo and send inline `html` per send. Rejected: makes the provider pure transport, but drags placeholder interpolation and HTML escaping into Elixir, ships rendered blobs alongside the Phoenix release, and forfeits Resend's draft/publish/versioning machinery.

(End of file - total 33 lines)
</content>

- Reach enforces module boundaries in `.reach.exs`: web→Repo only via `DhcWeb.Plugs.MagicLinkRateLimit`, Stripe only via `Dhc.Stripe.Operations.*` (never `Dhc.Stripe.Client.request/1`), Nostrum only inside `Dhc.Discord.*`, Req as the only HTTP client, no `IO.puts` outside Mix tasks/`Dhc.Release`. New findings fail the build; baseline known transitional findings with `MIX_ENV=dev mix reach.check --arch --write-baseline .reach-baseline.json`
- Keep generated Stripe modules under `lib/dhc/stripe/generated/` excluded from Credo instead of refactoring generated source
- Use the already included and available `:req` (`Req`) library for HTTP requests, **avoid** `:httpoison`, `:tesla`, and `:httpc`. Req is included by default and is the preferred HTTP client for Phoenix apps
- **Documented exception (ADR 0021)**: transactional email goes through Swoosh, whose api client is `config :swoosh, api_client: Dhc.Email.ApiClient` wrapping `Swoosh.ApiClient.Finch` over a named `{Finch, name: Swoosh.Finch}` child in `Dhc.Application`. Finch is already a production dependency, so Hackney stays out of prod. Application code outside `Dhc.Email.*` still uses Req everywhere else.
- Hackney is test-only because Testcontainers requires its 1.x Unix-socket transport. Keep it out of production and do not force Hackney 4 until Testcontainers supports Docker Unix sockets with it; the matching Hackney advisory exceptions in `mix.exs` apply only to that test dependency.
- Nostrum's REST client pulls Gun and Cowlib into production. Limit Cowlib advisory exceptions to explicitly reviewed CVE IDs and document the relevant exposure or mitigation in `mix.exs`; re-evaluate CVE-2026-43971 before adding Link-header serialization or passing untrusted targets, `rel` values, or attribute keys to `cow_link:link/1`.

### Phoenix v1.8 guidelines

- **Always** begin your LiveView templates with `<Layouts.app flash={@flash} ...>` which wraps all inner content
- The `MyAppWeb.Layouts` module is aliased in the `my_app_web.ex` file, so you can use it without needing to alias it again
- Anytime you run into errors with no `current_scope` assign:
  - You failed to follow the Authenticated Routes guidelines, or you failed to pass `current_scope` to `<Layouts.app>`
  - **Always** fix the `current_scope` error by moving your routes to the proper `live_session` and ensure you pass `current_scope` as needed
- Phoenix v1.8 moved the `<.flash_group>` component to the `Layouts` module. You are **forbidden** from calling `<.flash_group>` outside of the `layouts.ex` module
- Out of the box, `core_components.ex` imports an `<.icon name="hero-x-mark" class="w-5 h-5"/>` component for hero icons. **Always** use the `<.icon>` component for icons, **never** use `Heroicons` modules or similar
- **Always** use the imported `<.input>` component for form inputs from `core_components.ex` when available. `<.input>` is imported and using it will save steps and prevent errors
- If you override the default input classes (`<.input class="myclass px-2 py-1 rounded-lg">)`) class with your own values, no default classes are inherited, so your
custom classes must fully style the input

## Elixir guidelines

- Elixir lists **do not support index based access via the access syntax**

  **Never do this (invalid)**:

      i = 0
      mylist = ["blue", "green"]
      mylist[i]

  Instead, **always** use `Enum.at`, pattern matching, or `List` for index based list access, ie:

      i = 0
      mylist = ["blue", "green"]
      Enum.at(mylist, i)

- Elixir variables are immutable, but can be rebound, so for block expressions like `if`, `case`, `cond`, etc
  you *must* bind the result of the expression to a variable if you want to use it and you CANNOT rebind the result inside the expression, ie:

      # INVALID: we are rebinding inside the `if` and the result never gets assigned
      if connected?(socket) do
        socket = assign(socket, :val, val)
      end

      # VALID: we rebind the result of the `if` to a new variable
      socket =
        if connected?(socket) do
          assign(socket, :val, val)
        end

- **Never** nest multiple modules in the same file as it can cause cyclic dependencies and compilation errors
- **Never** use map access syntax (`changeset[:field]`) on structs as they do not implement the Access behaviour by default. For regular structs, you **must** access the fields directly, such as `my_struct.field` or use higher level APIs that are available on the struct if they exist, `Ecto.Changeset.get_field/2` for changesets
- Elixir's standard library has everything necessary for date and time manipulation. Familiarize yourself with the common `Time`, `Date`, `DateTime`, and `Calendar` interfaces by accessing their documentation as necessary. **Never** install additional dependencies unless asked or for date/time parsing (which you can use the `date_time_parser` package)
- Don't use `String.to_atom/1` on user input (memory leak risk)
- Predicate function names should not start with `is_` and should end in a question mark. Names like `is_thing` should be reserved for guards
- Elixir's builtin OTP primitives like `DynamicSupervisor` and `Registry`, require names in the child spec, such as `{DynamicSupervisor, name: MyApp.MyDynamicSup}`, then you can use `DynamicSupervisor.start_child(MyApp.MyDynamicSup, child_spec)`
- Use `Task.async_stream(collection, callback, options)` for concurrent enumeration with back-pressure. The majority of times you will want to pass `timeout: :infinity` as option

## Mix guidelines

- Read the docs and options before using tasks (by using `mix help task_name`)
- To debug test failures, run tests in a specific file with `mix test test/my_test.exs` or run all previously failed tests with `mix test --failed`
- `mix deps.clean --all` is **almost never needed**. **Avoid** using it unless you have good reason

## Test guidelines

- **Always use `start_supervised!/1`** to start processes in tests as it guarantees cleanup between tests
- **Avoid** `Process.sleep/1` and `Process.alive?/1` in tests
  - Instead of sleeping to wait for a process to finish, **always** use `Process.monitor/1` and assert on the DOWN message:

      ref = Process.monitor(pid)
      assert_receive {:DOWN, ^ref, :process, ^pid, :normal}

   - Instead of sleeping to synchronize before the next call, **always** use `_ = :sys.get_state/1` to ensure the process has handled prior messages
<!-- phoenix:elixir-end -->

<!-- phoenix:phoenix-start -->
## Phoenix guidelines

- Remember Phoenix router `scope` blocks include an optional alias which is prefixed for all routes within the scope. **Always** be mindful of this when creating routes within a scope to avoid duplicate module prefixes.

- You **never** need to create your own `alias` for route definitions! The `scope` provides the alias, ie:

      scope "/admin", AppWeb.Admin do
        pipe_through :browser

        live "/users", UserLive, :index
      end

  the UserLive route would point to the `AppWeb.Admin.UserLive` module

- `Phoenix.View` no longer is needed or included with Phoenix, don't use it
<!-- phoenix:phoenix-end -->

<!-- phoenix:ecto-start -->
## Ecto Guidelines

- **Always** preload Ecto associations in queries when they'll be accessed in templates, ie a message that needs to reference the `message.user.email`
- Remember `import Ecto.Query` and other supporting modules when you write `seeds.exs`
- `Ecto.Schema` fields always use the `:string` type, even for `:text`, columns, ie: `field :name, :string`
- `Ecto.Changeset.validate_number/2` **DOES NOT SUPPORT the `:allow_nil` option**. By default, Ecto validations only run if a change for the given field exists and the change value is not nil, so such as option is never needed
- You **must** use `Ecto.Changeset.get_field(changeset, :field)` to access changeset fields
- Fields which are set programmatically, such as `user_id`, must not be listed in `cast` calls or similar for security purposes. Instead they must be explicitly set when creating the struct
- **Always** invoke `mix ecto.gen.migration migration_name_using_underscores` when generating migration files, so the correct timestamp and conventions are applied
<!-- phoenix:ecto-end -->

<!-- usage-rules-end -->

1: defmodule Dhc.Email.Worker do
2:   @moduledoc """
3:   Oban worker that sends transactional emails through the Swoosh transport
4:   seam (ADR 0021 — Swoosh Is the Email Transport Seam).
5: 
6:   Migrated from the `process-emails` Deno edge function. Each job represents
7:   a single email (one Oban job per message, replacing the pgmq batch-read
8:   pattern).
9: 
10:   ## Job args (public contract — unchanged)
11: 
12:     * `email` — the recipient email address
13:     * `transactional_id` — a friendly template name (`"inviteMember"`,
14:       `"workshopAnnouncement"`, `"workshopRegistration"`,
15:       `"workshopRegistrationError"`, `"magicLink"`). The worker translates
16:       this to the provider's dashboard-generated template ID via the
17:       `:loops_transactional_ids` app env map.
18:     * `data_variables` — key-value pairs injected into the email template
19:       (values must be strings or numbers)
20: 
21:   ## Delivery
22: 
23:   The worker builds one `%Swoosh.Email{}` per job — recipient, sender, and
24:   provider options (`transactional_id`, `data_variables`) — and hands it to
25:   `Dhc.Email.Mailer`. Which provider actually delivers is environment config,
26:   not code: `Swoosh.Adapters.Loops` in prod, `Swoosh.Adapters.Mailpit` over
27:   HTTP in dev (`http://localhost:8025` web UI), `Swoosh.Adapters.Test` in
28:   tests.
29: 
30:   Outside prod the message is decorated with a JSON summary body
31:   (recipient + friendly Kind + data variables) so the dev inbox shows who
32:   would receive what; providers render real bodies from their templates.
33: 
34:   ## Idempotency
35: 
36:   Every send carries an `Idempotency-Key` derived from the Oban job id
37:   (`oban-<job.id>`), applied at the HTTP layer by `Dhc.Email.ApiClient`.
38:   Provider retries therefore cannot double-send a delivered email.
39: 
40:   ## Error classification
41: 
42:     * Invalid job args and unmapped/empty template IDs are deterministic:
43:       the job is **cancelled immediately** (`{:cancel, _}`) with a Sentry
44:       capture instead of burning five identical attempts.
45:     * In prod, provider responses of 4xx (except 429 rate limiting) are
46:       deterministic rejections too: cancelled with Sentry capture. Rate
47:       limits, 5xx, and network errors are transient: returned as
48:       `{:error, reason}` for Oban's exponential-backoff retries
49:       (`max_attempts: 5`).
50:     * Outside prod, delivery failures are logged and swallowed (`:ok`) —
51:       a stopped Mailpit container must never fail or retry dev jobs.
52: 
53:   ## Logging
54: 
55:   Every log line carries the Oban job context (`oban_job_id`, `oban_attempt`,
56:   `oban_queue`, `oban_worker`) plus `email` and `transactional_id`, so
57:   failures can be correlated to a specific job.
58:   """
59: 
60:   use Oban.Worker, queue: :emails, max_attempts: 5
61: 
62:   require Logger
63: 
64:   alias Dhc.Email.Mailer
65:   alias Swoosh.Email
66: 
67:   @transactional_ids ~w(inviteMember workshopAnnouncement workshopRegistration workshopRegistrationError magicLink)
68:   @idempotency_header "Idempotency-Key"
69: 
70:   @impl Worker
71:   def perform(%Oban.Job{args: args} = job) do
72:     ctx = job_log_context(job)
73: 
74:     with :ok <- validate_args(args, ctx),
75:          :ok <- deliver(args, job, ctx) do
76:       :ok
77:     else
78:       {:cancel, _reason} = cancelled -> cancelled
79:       {:error, _reason} = retryable -> retryable
80:     end
81:   end
82: 
83:   # -- Argument validation ----------------------------------------------------
84: 
85:   defp validate_args(args, ctx) do
86:     errors =
87:       []
88:       |> validate_required(args, "email")
89:       |> validate_email_format(args)
90:       |> validate_required(args, "transactional_id")
91:       |> validate_transactional_id(args)
92:       |> validate_data_variables(args)
93: 
94:     case errors do
95:       [] ->
96:         :ok
97: 
98:       errors ->
99:         message = "Invalid email job args: #{Enum.join(errors, ", ")}"
100: 
101:         Logger.error(
102:           "[email-worker] #{message}",
103:           Keyword.merge(ctx,
104:             email: args["email"],
105:             transactional_id: args["transactional_id"],
106:             validation_errors: Enum.join(errors, ", ")
107:           )
108:         )
109: 
110:         capture_deterministic_failure(message, ctx,
111:           args: args,
112:           validation_errors: errors
113:         )
114: 
115:         {:cancel, {:validation, errors}}
116:     end
117:   end
118: 
119:   defp validate_required(errors, args, field) do
120:     if is_nil(args[field]) or args[field] == "" do
121:       ["missing #{field}" | errors]
122:     else
123:       errors
124:     end
125:   end
126: 
127:   defp validate_email_format(errors, %{"email" => email}) when is_binary(email) do
128:     if email =~ ~r/^[^\s@]+@[^\s@]+\.[^\s@]+$/ do
129:       errors
130:     else
131:       ["invalid email format" | errors]
132:     end
133:   end
134: 
135:   defp validate_email_format(errors, _args), do: errors
136: 
137:   defp validate_transactional_id(errors, %{"transactional_id" => id})
138:        when id in @transactional_ids,
139:        do: errors
140: 
141:   defp validate_transactional_id(errors, _args),
142:     do: ["invalid transactional_id" | errors]
143: 
144:   defp validate_data_variables(errors, %{"data_variables" => vars}) when is_map(vars) do
145:     invalid_values =
146:       Enum.any?(vars, fn
147:         {_k, v} when is_binary(v) -> false
148:         {_k, v} when is_number(v) -> false
149:         _ -> true
150:       end)
151: 
152:     if invalid_values do
153:       ["data_variables values must be strings or numbers" | errors]
154:     else
155:       errors
156:     end
157:   end
158: 
159:   defp validate_data_variables(errors, _args), do: errors
160: 
161:   # -- Delivery ----------------------------------------------------------------
162: 
163:   defp deliver(
164:          %{"email" => recipient, "transactional_id" => kind} = args,
165:          %Oban.Job{} = job,
166:          ctx
167:        ) do
168:     with {:ok, template_id} <- resolve_template_id(kind, ctx) do
169:       data_variables = Map.get(args, "data_variables", %{})
170: 
171:       recipient
172:       |> build_email(kind, template_id, data_variables, job.id)
173:       |> deliver_email(kind, ctx)
174:     end
175:   end
176: 
177:   defp resolve_template_id(friendly_name, ctx) do
178:     # Translation mirrors the edge function's env-var lookup. The map is built
179:     # in config/runtime.exs / config/dev.exs from *_TRANSACTIONAL_ID env vars.
180:     # We never send the friendly name to the provider (it 404s there); an
181:     # unmapped or empty mapping is a deterministic configuration failure.
182:     map = Application.get_env(:dhc, :loops_transactional_ids, %{})
183: 
184:     case Map.get(map, friendly_name) do
185:       template_id when is_binary(template_id) and template_id != "" ->
186:         {:ok, template_id}
187: 
188:       _ ->
189:         message = "No template ID mapped for transactional_id"
190: 
191:         Logger.error(
192:           "[email-worker] #{message}",
193:           Keyword.merge(ctx, transactional_id: friendly_name)
194:         )
195: 
196:         capture_deterministic_failure(message, ctx,
197:           transactional_id: friendly_name
198:         )
199: 
200:         {:cancel, {:transactional_id_not_configured, friendly_name}}
201:     end
202:   end
203: 
204:   defp build_email(recipient, kind, template_id, data_variables, oban_job_id) do
205:     email =
206:       Email.new()
207:       |> Email.from(email_from())
208:       |> Email.to(recipient)
209:       |> Email.put_provider_option(:transactional_id, template_id)
210:       |> Email.put_provider_option(:data_variables, data_variables)
211: 
212:     if oban_job_id do
213:       key = "oban-#{oban_job_id}"
214: 
215:       email
216:       |> Email.put_provider_option(:idempotency_key, key)
217:       # MIME-level copy for dev-inbox observability; the wire header comes from
218:       # the provider option via Dhc.Email.ApiClient.
219:       |> Email.header(@idempotency_header, key)
220:     else
221:       email
222:     end
223:     |> decorate_for_dev(recipient, kind, data_variables)
224:   end
225: 
226:   # Non-prod only: providers render real bodies from their templates, so the
227:   # dev inbox gets a JSON summary (recipient + friendly Kind + variables).
228:   defp decorate_for_dev(email, recipient, kind, data_variables) do
229:     if env() == :prod do
230:       email
231:     else
232:       payload = %{
233:         email: recipient,
234:         transactional_id: kind,
235:         data_variables: data_variables
236:       }
237: 
238:       subject = "[dev] Email: #{kind}"
239:       body = Jason.encode!(payload, pretty: true)
240: 
241:       email
242:       |> Email.subject(subject)
243:       |> Email.text_body(body)
244:     end
245:   end
246: 
247:   defp deliver_email(%Email{} = email, kind, ctx) do
248:     case Mailer.deliver(email) do
249:       {:ok, receipt} ->
250:         Logger.info(
251:           "[email-worker] Email sent successfully",
252:           Keyword.merge(ctx,
253:             email: recipient_address(email),
254:             transactional_id: kind,
255:             receipt: inspect(receipt)
256:           )
257:         )
258: 
259:         :ok
260: 
261:       {:error, reason} ->
262:         handle_delivery_error(reason, kind, ctx)
263:     end
264:   end
265: 
266:   defp handle_delivery_error(reason, kind, ctx) do
267:     if env() == :prod do
268:       classify_delivery_error(reason, kind, ctx)
269:     else
270:       Logger.warning(
271:         "[email-worker] Dev relay delivery failed (is `docker compose up -d mailpit` running?), job will not retry",
272:         Keyword.merge(ctx,
273:           transactional_id: kind,
274:           reason: inspect(reason)
275:         )
276:       )
277: 
278:       :ok
279:     end
280:   end
281: 
282:   # Deterministic rejections (4xx except rate limiting): retrying cannot fix a
283:   # bad payload or template mapping, so cancel immediately with a Sentry
284:   # capture rather than burn all attempts.
285:   defp classify_delivery_error({status, _body}, kind, ctx)
286:        when is_integer(status) and status >= 400 and status < 500 and status != 429 do
287:     message = "Provider rejected #{kind}; discarding job"
288: 
289:     Logger.error(
290:       "[email-worker] #{message}",
291:       Keyword.merge(ctx,
292:         transactional_id: kind,
293:         provider_status: status
294:       )
295:     )
296: 
297:     capture_deterministic_failure(message, ctx,
298:       transactional_id: kind,
299:       provider_status: status
300:     )
301: 
302:     {:cancel, {:provider_rejected, status}}
303:   end
304: 
305:   # Rate limits (429), 5xx, and network errors are transient — let Oban retry
306:   # with backoff. The Idempotency-Key makes those retries safe against
307:   # double-sends that were already accepted.
308:   defp classify_delivery_error(reason, kind, ctx) do
309:     Logger.error(
310:       "[email-worker] Transient delivery failure; Oban will retry",
311:       Keyword.merge(ctx,
312:         transactional_id: kind,
313:         reason: inspect(reason)
314:       )
315:     )
316: 
317:     {:error, reason}
318:   end
319: 
320:   # -- Environment & helpers ---------------------------------------------------
321: 
322:   defp env do
323:     Application.get_env(:dhc, :environment, :development)
324:   end
325: 
326:   # Sentry capture for deterministic failures (invalid args, unmapped template
327:   # IDs, provider rejections). Oban context rides in :extra as a flat map —
328:   # this Sentry version does not accept :contexts.
329:   defp capture_deterministic_failure(message, ctx, extra) do
330:     Sentry.capture_message(message,
331:       level: :error,
332:       extra:
333:         Map.merge(Map.new(extra), %{
334:           oban_job_id: ctx[:oban_job_id],
335:           oban_attempt: ctx[:oban_attempt],
336:           oban_queue: ctx[:oban_queue],
337:           oban_worker: ctx[:oban_worker]
338:         })
339:     )
340:   end
341: 
342:   # Swoosh requires a sender on every message. Loops ignores it (templates
343:   # define the sender); Mailpit shows it in the dev inbox.
344:   defp email_from do
345:     Application.get_env(:dhc, :email_from, "dev@dhc.local")
346:   end
347: 
348:   defp recipient_address(%Email{to: [{_, recipient}]}) when is_binary(recipient),
349:     do: recipient
350: 
351:   defp recipient_address(%Email{to: to}), do: inspect(to)
352: 
353:   defp job_log_context(%Oban.Job{} = job) do
354:     [
355:       oban_job_id: job.id,
356:       oban_attempt: job.attempt,
357:       oban_queue: job.queue,
358:       oban_worker: job.worker
359:     ]
360:   end
361: end

191:   # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
192:   # Seam 2: delivery-failure semantics. The mailer adapter is swapped for a
193:   # configurable stub (mirroring the :discord_adapter / :onboarding_stripe_adapter
194:   # seams) so classification can be exercised without real HTTP.
195:   # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
196: 
197:   describe "perform/1 failure semantics in prod" do
198:     import ExUnit.CaptureLog
199: 
200:     setup do
201:       Application.put_env(:dhc, :environment, :prod)
202:       :ok
203:     end
204: 
205:     test "cancels deterministically when the provider rejects a 4xx validation family response" do

# Research: Swoosh.Adapters.Resend (Swoosh 1.27.1)

Research-only. No files were edited.

## 1. Swoosh version in this repo

| Source | Value |
|---|---|
| `apps/phoenix/mix.exs` line 92 | `{:swoosh, "~> 1.26"}` |
| `apps/phoenix/mix.lock` line 76 | `"swoosh": {:hex, :swoosh, "1.27.1", ...}` |
| Resend adapter introduced | **1.27.0** (PR [#1089](https://github.com/swoosh/swoosh/pull/1089)) — first release that ships `Swoosh.Adapters.Resend` |
| 1.27.1 changelog | Bug fix to `Swoosh.Adapters.AmazonSES` only; the Resend adapter is unchanged between 1.27.0 and 1.27.1 |

So the resolver pulls in **1.27.1**, which is the first Swoosh version in which `Swoosh.Adapters.Resend` exists. There is no `Swoosh.Adapters.Resend` in 1.26.x or earlier; the adapter cannot be used without bumping the lock — `~> 1.26` already does so.

> Repo context note (for the agent, not part of the research deliverable): `apps/phoenix/AGENTS.md` ADR 0021 currently names **Loops** as the prod adapter, **Mailpit** in dev, **Test** in tests. Resend is therefore a future/in-flight swap, not the live prod adapter.

## 2. Production configuration

`Swoosh.Adapters.Resend` declares `use Swoosh.Adapter, required_config: [:api_key]`. The module attributes and config behaviour:

```elixir
@base_url      "https://api.resend.com"
@api_endpoint  "/emails"
@batch_endpoint "/emails/batch"

defp base_url(config), do: config[:base_url] || @base_url
```

So a production-shaped config is exactly two keys per environment, plus the standard `local: false` in prod:

```elixir
# config/config.exs
config :swoosh, api_client: Dhc.Email.ApiClient   # already in repo (ADR 0021)

# config/prod.exs
config :dhc, Dhc.Email.Mailer,
  adapter: Swoosh.Adapters.Resend,
  api_key: System.fetch_env!("RESEND_API_KEY")

# config/prod.exs (one-liner) — alternatively defer the api_key to runtime.exs:
# config :dhc, Dhc.Email.Mailer, adapter: Swoosh.Adapters.Resend
# config/runtime.exs:
#   config :dhc, Dhc.Email.Mailer, api_key: System.fetch_env!("RESEND_API_KEY")

config :swoosh, local: false
```

Optional config keys recognised by the adapter (forwarded to `prepare_request_headers/2` and `base_url/1`):

| Key | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `:api_key` *(required)* | — | `re_…`; sent as `Authorization: Bearer <key>`. |
| `:base_url` | `"https://api.resend.com"` | Override only for the EU region (`"https://eu-api.resend.com"`) or a self-hosted gateway. |

There is no `:api_url`, no separate `:endpoint`, no extra region/sender config on the adapter itself.

Because the adapter calls `Swoosh.ApiClient.post/4` (not Hackney/Tesla), it will route through the existing `Dhc.Email.ApiClient` wrapper over `{Finch, name: Swoosh.Finch}` set up in `Dhc.Application` — Finch is already a prod dep, so no extra HTTP-client dependency is introduced (consistent with ADR 0021's rationale).

## 3. `Swoosh.Email` provider_options shape for a Resend hosted template by alias + variables + idempotency key

The four provider options recognised by the adapter are exactly:

| Atom key | Wire field | Type / shape | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `:tags` | `"tags"` | `[%{name: binary, value: binary}, …]` | Max 256 chars per value. |
| `:scheduled_at` | `"scheduled_at"` | ISO 8601 binary (`"2024-08-05T11:52:01.858Z"`) | Not supported in batch. |
| `:idempotency_key` | `Idempotency-Key` **header** | binary | Sent as HTTP header by the adapter itself — *not* a JSON body field. |
| `:template` | `"template"` | `%{id: binary, variables: map \| nil}` | `id` may be the dashboard-generated ID **or the template alias** (the adapter does not differentiate; both go straight into `id`). |

Wire body shape produced by the adapter for a templated send:

```json
{
  "from": "Sender Name <sender@resend.dev>",
  "to": ["recipient@example.com"],
  "subject": "optional subject override",
  "template": { "id": "my-alias", "variables": { "name": "Ada", "action_url": "https://example.com" } }
}
```

…with these request headers (from `prepare_request_headers/2`):

```
Authorization:    Bearer <api_key>
Content-Type:     application/json
User-Agent:       swoosh/<Swoosh.version()>
Idempotency-Key:  <provider_options[:idempotency_key]>   # only if set
```

Constraints called out in the adapter's `@moduledoc`:

- When `:template` is set, you **must not** send `html_body` or `text_body` on the same email — the adapter does not strip them, it just renders `html`/`text` keys into the body alongside `template`, which Resend will reject.
- The template's `from`, `subject`, and `reply_to` can be overridden by setting the corresponding `Swoosh.Email` fields on the email struct (the adapter always writes `from`/`subject`/`reply_to` if non-empty, and Resend accepts template overrides on those three).
- `:template.variables` must be a plain map of `key => value` pairs (matches the Resend API; Swoosh does no validation here).

### Canonical code example (template-by-alias + variables + idempotency key)

```elixir
import Swoosh.Email

new()

## 4. Response / error shapes (worker-classification relevance)

The adapter's `deliver/2` (lib/swoosh/adapters/resend.ex) returns one of three shapes:

```elixir
{:ok, %{id: binary}}                   # any 2xx–3xx; "id" is Resend's message id
{:error, {status_integer, body}}       # any 4xx–5xx; body is the decoded JSON map,
                                       #   or the raw response string if JSON decode fails
{:error, reason}                       # transport-level (Finch / Req / Hackney) failure
```

Concrete examples:

- 2xx body `{"id":"abc-123"}` → `{:ok, %{id: "abc-123"}}`.
- 422 from Resend → `{:error, {422, %{"statusCode" => 422, "name" => "validation_error", "message" => "…", "messageData" => %{…}}}}`.
- 429 → `{:error, {429, …}}` (transient — retry).
- 5xx → `{:error, {500, …}}` (transient — retry).
- Finch `Mint.TransportError` → `{:error, %Mint.TransportError{reason: :closed}}` or `{:error, :timeout}` etc.

### Compatibility with the existing worker's classification (apps/phoenix/lib/dhc/email/workers/worker.ex)

The worker classifies with `defp classify_delivery_error({status, _body}, …) when is_integer(status) and status >= 400 and status < 500 and status != 429`. The Resend adapter's `{:error, {status, _body}}` shape matches this clause exactly — no worker changes needed for shape compatibility. The catch-all `{:error, reason} → retryable` covers transport failures.

Two adapter-specific observations that *will* affect the worker if/when Resend becomes the prod adapter:

1. **Idempotency-Key is now set by the adapter itself** (from `email.provider_options[:idempotency_key]`), not only by the `Dhc.Email.ApiClient` wrapper. Today the worker also sets `Email.header(@idempotency_header, key)` (decorative) and the API client attaches it at the HTTP layer; with the Resend adapter, `Dhc.Email.ApiClient` is redundant for this header — the adapter handles it. If the wrapper sets the header too, the value will be duplicated; if Finch's underlying Mint respects HTTP/2's single-value rule for known headers, the second one wins. The worker comment on line 36–38 should be updated.
2. **The Loops-shaped provider options (`:transactional_id` + `:data_variables`) used in `build_email/5`** are provider-specific to Loops. Resend's adapter silently ignores unknown keys in `provider_options` (it pattern-matches only on `:tags`, `:scheduled_at`, `:idempotency_key`, `:template`), so swapping adapters without renaming those keys would silently send nothing — the worker would build a valid email but with an empty body and no template. Resend's equivalent key names are `:template => %{id: …, variables: …}`.

1: defmodule Dhc.Email.ApiClient do
2:   @moduledoc """
3:   Swoosh api_client that adds an Idempotency-Key HTTP header to every
4:   outgoing provider request (ADR 0021).
5: 
6:   Swoosh's first-party adapters hard-code their HTTP request headers, so an
7:   `Idempotency-Key` set via `Swoosh.Email.header/3` never reaches the wire.
8:   This client wraps `Swoosh.ApiClient.Finch` and lifts the
9:   `:idempotency_key` provider option onto the request instead:
10: 
11:       email
12:       |> put_provider_option(:idempotency_key, "oban-1234")
13:       |> Dhc.Email.Mailer.deliver()
14:       # => POST with header {"Idempotency-Key", "oban-1234"}
15: 
16:   Because it sits below the adapter layer, the header survives the Loops →
17:   Resend cutover unchanged. Remove this wrapper if upstream Swoosh ever grows
18:   first-party idempotency support.
19: 
20:   Wired globally via `config :swoosh, api_client: Dhc.Email.ApiClient`; the
21:   Finch instance is named by `config :swoosh, :finch_name` (default
22:   `Swoosh.Finch`, supervised in `Dhc.Application`).
23:   """
24: 
25:   @behaviour Swoosh.ApiClient
26: 
27:   @header_name "Idempotency-Key"
28: 
29:   @impl true
30:   def init, do: Swoosh.ApiClient.Finch.init()
31: 
32:   @impl true
33:   def post(url, headers, body, %Swoosh.Email{} = email) do
34:     Swoosh.ApiClient.Finch.post(url, idempotency_header(headers, email), body, email)
35:   end
36: 
37:   @doc """
38:   Prepends `{"Idempotency-Key", key}` to `headers` when `email` carries the
39:   `:idempotency_key` provider option; returns `headers` untouched otherwise.
40:   """
41:   @spec idempotency_header(Swoosh.ApiClient.headers(), Swoosh.Email.t()) ::
42:           Swoosh.ApiClient.headers()
43:   def idempotency_header(headers, %Swoosh.Email{provider_options: provider_options}) do
44:     case provider_options[:idempotency_key] do
45:       nil -> headers
46:       key when is_binary(key) -> [{@header_name, key} | headers]
47:     end
48:   end
49: end

1: /**
2:  * Template metadata schema for the code-authored transactional email
3:  * templates (ADR 0022 — Code-Authored Templates Synced to Resend-Hosted
4:  * Templates).
5:  *
6:  * Each component file in `emails/` exports its metadata via
7:  * {@link defineTemplate}, making TypeScript the single schema authority for
8:  * what each Email Kind requires: default subject, default sender, and the
9:  * declared typed variables. The Elixir side keeps only its generic
10:  * string|number validation and Resend enforces the per-template variable
11:  * contract at send time.
12:  *
13:  * Constraints encoded here mirror Resend's template rules:
14:  *
15:  * - variable keys are UPPER_SNAKE and referenced as {{{KEY}}} in markup;
16:  * - at most 20 declared variables per template;
17:  * - reserved names cannot be declared.
18:  *
19:  * The fallback/type correlation is expressed statically through the
20:  * {@link TemplateVariable} discriminated union, so an invalid pairing fails
21:  * compilation instead of validation.
22:  */
23: 
24: /** The five whitelisted Email Kinds — mirrors `@transactional_ids` in `Dhc.Email.Worker`. */
25: export const EMAIL_KINDS = [
26:   "inviteMember",
27:   "workshopAnnouncement",
28:   "workshopRegistration",
29:   "workshopRegistrationError",
30:   "magicLink",
31: ] as const;
32: 
33: export type EmailKind = (typeof EMAIL_KINDS)[number];
34: 
35: interface VariableBase {
36:   /** UPPER_SNAKE key as declared on the Resend-hosted template (`{{{KEY}}}`). */
37:   readonly key: string;
38: }
39: 
40: export interface StringTemplateVariable extends VariableBase {
41:   readonly type: "string";
42:   /** Optional fallback rendered when a send omits the variable. */
43:   readonly fallback?: string;
44: }
45: 
46: export interface NumberTemplateVariable extends VariableBase {
47:   readonly type: "number";
48:   readonly fallback?: number;
49: }
50: 
51: export type TemplateVariable = StringTemplateVariable | NumberTemplateVariable;
52: 
53: export type TemplateVariableType = TemplateVariable["type"];
54: 
55: export interface TemplateMetadata {
56:   /** The stable provider-neutral Email Kind (`inviteMember`, …). */
57:   readonly kind: EmailKind;
58:   /** Kebab-case alias derived from the kind; Resend templates are addressed by it. */
59:   readonly alias: string;
60:   readonly subject: string;
61:   /** Default sender in `Name <addr>` form. */
62:   readonly from: string;
63:   readonly variables: readonly TemplateVariable[];
64: }
65: 
66: export interface TemplateDefinition {
67:   kind: EmailKind;
68:   subject: string;
69:   from: string;
70:   variables: readonly TemplateVariable[];
71: }
72: 
73: /** Names Resend reserves on every template; declaring them is an error. */
74: export const RESERVED_VARIABLE_NAMES = new Set([
75:   "FIRST_NAME",
76:   "LAST_NAME",
77:   "EMAIL",
78:   "RESEND_UNSUBSCRIBE_URL",
79:   "contact",
80:   "this",
81: ]);
82: 
83: /** Resend allows at most 20 declared variables per template. */
84: const MAX_VARIABLES = 20;
85: 
86: const UPPER_SNAKE = /^[A-Z][A-Z0-9]*(_[A-Z0-9]+)*$/;
87: const SENDER_WITH_ADDRESS = /<[^<>]+@[^<>]+\.[^<>]+>|^[^\s<]+@[^\s<]+\.[^\s<]+$/;
88: 
89: /**
90:  * Derives the kebab-case template alias of an Email Kind. Sends address the
91:  * Resend-hosted template by this alias, so no kind→ID configuration map ever
92:  * exists at runtime (ADR 0022).
93:  */
94: export function templateAlias(kind: string): string {
95:   return kind.replace(/([a-z0-9])([A-Z])/g, "$1-$2").toLowerCase();
96: }
97: 
98: function validate(definition: TemplateDefinition): void {
99:   const { kind, subject, from, variables } = definition;
100: 
101:   if (subject.trim() === "") {
102:     throw new Error(`Template "${kind}" must declare a non-empty subject`);
103:   }
104: 
105:   if (!SENDER_WITH_ADDRESS.test(from)) {
106:     throw new Error(`Template "${kind}" must declare a "from" sender ("Name <addr>" or "addr")`);
107:   }
108: 
109:   if (variables.length > MAX_VARIABLES) {
110:     throw new Error(
111:       `Template "${kind}" declares ${variables.length} variables; Resend allows at most ${MAX_VARIABLES}`,
112:     );
113:   }
114: 
115:   const seen = new Set<string>();
116: 
117:   for (const { key } of variables) {
118:     if (!UPPER_SNAKE.test(key)) {
119:       throw new Error(
120:         `Template "${kind}" variable "${key}" must be UPPER_SNAKE (e.g. INVITATION_LINK)`,
121:       );
122:     }
123: 
124:     if (RESERVED_VARIABLE_NAMES.has(key.toUpperCase())) {
125:       throw new Error(`Template "${kind}" variable "${key}" is reserved by Resend`);
126:     }
127: 
128:     if (seen.has(key)) {
129:       throw new Error(`Template "${kind}" declares duplicate variable "${key}"`);
130:     }
131:     seen.add(key);
132:   }
133: }

Now I have a complete picture. Here's the comprehensive research report:

---

# Phoenix `Dhc.Email.Worker` Production Call-Site Research

## Summary

There are **exactly 4 production call sites** that construct `Dhc.Email.Worker` jobs across 3 Email Kinds. **`workshopRegistration` and `workshopRegistrationError` have no production call sites** — they are reserved, defined in the template package but never enqueued from Phoenix (the `workshop-registration.tsx` even comments "no production path enqueues this kind yet — it is a reserved name").

## Worker Contract (relevant excerpt)

- File: `apps/phoenix/lib/dhc/email/workers/worker.ex:1-67`
- `use Oban.Worker, queue: :emails, max_attempts: 5`
- Whitelisted `transactional_id` set (line 65): `~w(inviteMember workshopAnnouncement workshopRegistration workshopRegistrationError magicLink)`
- `data_variables` validation: values must be `string` or `number` (line 142-157); keys are not type-checked (Resend enforces the per-template contract at send time)
- `:idempotency_key` set as a Swoosh provider option and as the `Idempotency-Key` MIME header (line 187-190)

---

## 1. `inviteMember` — Two Call Sites

### Declared template variables (UPPER_SNAKE)
File: `packages/email-templates/emails/invite-member.tsx:29-33`
```
INVITEE_FIRST_NAME  string  fallback ""
INVITEE_LAST_NAME   string  fallback ""
INVITATION_LINK     string
```

### Call site A: `apps/phoenix/lib/dhc/invitations.ex:612-627`
```elixir
defp enqueue_invitation_email(invitation) do
  args = %{
    "email" => invitation.email,
    "transactional_id" => @invite_email_template,   # "inviteMember" (line 26)
    "data_variables" => %{
      "firstName" => invitation.first_name || "",
      "lastName" => invitation.last_name || "",
      "invitationLink" => invitation_link(invitation)
    }
  }

  case Oban.insert(EmailWorker.new(args)) do
    {:ok, _job} -> :ok
    {:error, reason} -> {:error, reason}
  end
end
```

**Mismatch:** the worker is sending **camelCase** keys (`firstName`, `lastName`, `invitationLink`) but the Resend-hosted template expects **UPPER_SNAKE** keys (`INVITEE_FIRST_NAME`, `INVITEE_LAST_NAME`, `INVITATION_LINK`). The template will not render the variables correctly — Resend will substitute empty strings for those `{{{KEY}}}` placeholders.

### Call site B: `apps/phoenix/lib/dhc/invitations/workers/bulk_invite_worker.ex:267-284`
```elixir
defp enqueue_invitation_email(invite_data, invitation_id) do
  invitation_link = invitation_link(invite_data, invitation_id)

  args = %{
    "email" => invite_data["email"],
    "transactional_id" => @invite_email_template,   # "inviteMember" (line 49)
    "data_variables" => %{
      "firstName" => invite_data["firstName"],
      "lastName" => invite_data["lastName"],
      "invitationLink" => invitation_link
    }
  }

  case Oban.insert(EmailWorker.new(args)) do
    {:ok, _job} -> :ok
    {:error, reason} -> {:error, {:email_enqueue, reason}}
  end
end
```

**Same mismatch** as Call site A: camelCase keys vs UPPER_SNAKE schema. `invitation_link` itself is well-formed (line 292-305: builds `app_url/members/signup/<id>?dateOfBirth=...&email=...`).

---

## 2. `workshopAnnouncement` — One Call Site

### Declared template variables (UPPER_SNAKE)
File: `packages/email-templates/emails/workshop-announcement.tsx:29-34`
```
MEMBER_FIRST_NAME  string  fallback "there"
MEMBER_LAST_NAME   string  fallback ""
MESSAGE            string
WORKSHOP_COUNT     number  fallback 0
```

### Call site C: `apps/phoenix/lib/dhc/workshop_announcements/workers/worker.ex:141-167`
```elixir
defp build_email_jobs(workshop, announcement_type) do
  if workshop.announce_email do
    message = WorkshopAnnouncements.format_email_message(workshop, announcement_type)
    users = WorkshopAnnouncements.list_active_users()    # %UserProfile{email, first_name, last_name}

    Logger.info(...)

    Enum.map(users, fn user ->
      EmailWorker.new(%{
        "email" => user.email,
        "transactional_id" => "workshopAnnouncement",
        "data_variables" => %{
          "first_name" => user.first_name,
          "last_name" => user.last_name,
          "message" => message,
          "workshop_count" => 1
        }
      })
    end)
  else
    []
  end
end
```

**Mismatch:** the worker is sending **snake_case** keys (`first_name`, `last_name`, `message`, `workshop_count`) but the Resend-hosted template expects **UPPER_SNAKE** keys (`MEMBER_FIRST_NAME`, `MEMBER_LAST_NAME`, `MESSAGE`, `WORKSHOP_COUNT`). Same problem as the invite path — Resend will substitute empty strings / `0` for the unrendered `{{{KEY}}}` placeholders.

`WorkshopAnnouncements.list_active_users/0` (file `apps/phoenix/lib/dhc/workshop_announcements.ex:72-86`) returns maps with `email`, `first_name`, `last_name` (no `nil` possible for `first_name`/`last_name` because the query selects directly from `user_profiles` columns).

---

## 3. `magicLink` — One Call Site

### Declared template variables (UPPER_SNAKE)
File: `packages/email-templates/emails/magic-link.tsx:23`
```
LOGIN_LINK  string
```

### Call site D: `apps/phoenix/lib/dhc/auth.ex:380-395`
```elixir
defp enqueue_magic_link_email(principal, url) do
  # ALE-165: ... The URL is passed as the `LoginLink` data variable —
  # the Loops "magic link" transactional template (`cma3yqgqw68tv9pm5v0si5ge3`)
  # renders `{{LoginLink}}`, so the key here must match the template.
  %{
    email: principal.email,
    transactional_id: "magicLink",
    data_variables: %{"LoginLink" => url}
  }
  |> Dhc.Email.Worker.new()
  |> Oban.insert()
end
```

**Partial mismatch (PascalCase):** the worker is sending **`LoginLink`** (PascalCase) but the Resend-hosted template expects **`LOGIN_LINK`** (UPPER_SNAKE). The inline comment in the file even acknowledges the legacy Loops variable name `{{LoginLink}}` and confirms the intent to match the template — but the schema-authoritative template file `magic-link.tsx` declares `LOGIN_LINK`, so the names are out of sync. Resend will not substitute the URL; the rendered email will show the fallback or empty.

**Note on shape:** this call site uses **atom keys** (`email:`, `transactional_id:`, `data_variables:`) instead of **string keys** like the other three call sites. The worker reads args with string keys (`args["email"]`, `args["transactional_id"]`, `args["data_variables"]`) and validates with `is_nil(args[field])` — atom-keyed maps will pass the `nil`/empty check for string fields only because `args["email"]` is `nil` for an atom-keyed map (then the `"missing email"` validation fires). However, the validation in `Dhc.Email.Worker` only checks the string keys; this call site would currently fail validation with "missing email" / "missing transactional_id" — yet the tests assert it works (`test/dhc_web/controllers/auth_session_controller_test.exs:496` checks the job is enqueued, not that the worker accepts the args). Worth flagging as a latent bug independent of the variable-name issue.

---

## Sender / From Configuration Used by Production

### Default fallback (config-driven, applies to ALL envs)
File: `apps/phoenix/config/config.exs:49-52`
```elixir
# Sender on outgoing messages. Providers render the real sender from their
# templates; this shows up in the dev Mailpit inbox and satisfies Swoosh's
# requirement for a from address.
config :dhc, :email_from, "dev@dhc.local"
```

### Read by the worker
File: `apps/phoenix/lib/dhc/email/workers/worker.ex:321-323`
```elixir
defp email_from do
  Application.get_env(:dhc, :email_from, "dev@dhc.local")
end
```
…then set on every outgoing `Swoosh.Email` (line 176: `Email.from(email_from())`).

### Production behavior
- `email_from` is **never overridden** for `:prod` in `config/prod.exs` or `config/runtime.exs` (grep confirms only one definition, in `config.exs`).
- Therefore, in production the wire-level `From:` header that Swoosh emits is **`dev@dhc.local`** — a clear mismatch with the `Dublin HEMA Club <no-reply@mail.dublinhemaclub.com>` sender declared by every template in `packages/email-templates/emails/*.tsx` (Resend overrides the visible sender from its hosted templates at the SMTP/receiving-MTA layer, but the outbound `From` envelope header still originates from this value).
- The per-template `from` declarations live in `packages/email-templates/src/template-metadata.ts:55-64` (`TemplateMetadata.from`) and are asserted in `defineTemplate` via `SENDER_WITH_ADDRESS` (line 87). For every kind the sender is the same:
  - `Dublin HEMA Club <no-reply@mail.dublinhemaclub.com>` (5/5 templates: `invite-member.tsx:28`, `workshop-announcement.tsx:28`, `workshop-registration.tsx:15`, `workshop-registration-error.tsx:15`, `magic-link.tsx:22`)
- Swoosh adapter used in production: `Swoosh.Adapters.Resend`, set in `config/runtime.exs:144-148`:
  ```elixir
  config :dhc, Dhc.Email.Mailer,
    adapter: Swoosh.Adapters.Resend,
    api_key: System.fetch_env!("RESEND_API_KEY")
  ```
  Swoosh API client override: `config :swoosh, api_client: Dhc.Email.ApiClient` (`config.exs:44-45`) — wires the `Idempotency-Key` header through `Dhc.Email.ApiClient` (`apps/phoenix/lib/dhc/email/api_client.ex:1-54`).

---

## Cross-Reference: Production Call Sites vs UPPER_SNAKE Schema

| Call site | `transactional_id` | `data_variables` keys sent | Schema UPPER_SNAKE keys | Match? |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `apps/phoenix/lib/dhc/invitations.ex:616-620` | `inviteMember` | `firstName`, `lastName`, `invitationLink` | `INVITEE_FIRST_NAME`, `INVITEE_LAST_NAME`, `INVITATION_LINK` | **NO** (camelCase) |
| `apps/phoenix/lib/dhc/invitations/workers/bulk_invite_worker.ex:273-277` | `inviteMember` | `firstName`, `lastName`, `invitationLink` | `INVITEE_FIRST_NAME`, `INVITEE_LAST_NAME`, `INVITATION_LINK` | **NO** (camelCase) |
| `apps/phoenix/lib/dhc/workshop_announcements/workers/worker.ex:156-161` | `workshopAnnouncement` | `first_name`, `last_name`, `message`, `workshop_count` | `MEMBER_FIRST_NAME`, `MEMBER_LAST_NAME`, `MESSAGE`, `WORKSHOP_COUNT` | **NO** (snake_case) |
| `apps/phoenix/lib/dhc/auth.ex:388-393` | `magicLink` | `LoginLink` (atom-keyed map) | `LOGIN_LINK` | **NO** (PascalCase + atom keys) |

**Net result:** every production path that enqueues an `Email.Worker` job sends variables under a casing that does not match the UPPER_SNAKE keys declared in `packages/email-templates`. The migration to Resend-hosted templates (ADR 0022) is incomplete on the Elixir send path — the validation in `Dhc.Email.Worker` only checks value types, not key casing, so the bugs are silent at enqueue time and only become visible as empty/blank substitutions in the rendered emails.

1: defmodule Dhc.Invitations.BulkInviteWorkerTest do

15:   # ALE-162 (ADR 0010): issue time is side-effect free. The worker no longer
16:   # calls the Supabase admin API, creates a Stripe customer, or inserts a
17:   # user_profiles row. It only:
18:   #   - mints a fresh Phoenix UUID for invitation.prospective_principal_id;
19:   #   - inserts the pending invitation carrying first/last/phone/DOB;
20:   #   - enqueues the inviteMember email;
21:   #   - marks the waitlist entry invited (when the invite came from a waitlist).
22:   #
23:   # Acceptance (not the worker) materializes the Principal + UserProfile +
24:   # MemberProfile + role. Acceptance creates the Stripe customer; pricing is
25:   # read-only.
26: 
27:   describe "perform/1 validation" do
28:     test "returns validation errors when invites are missing" do
29:       assert {:error, {:validation, errors}} =
30:                BulkInviteWorker.perform(%Oban.Job{
31:                  args: %{"user" => %{"id" => Ecto.UUID.generate()}}
32:                })
33:

35:     end

39:

41:       assert "invites must be a non-empty list" in errors
42:     end

45:       args = %{"invites" => [%{"email" => "member@example.com"}], "user" => %{}}
46:

48:       assert "user.id is required" in errors
49:     end
50:   end

52:   describe "perform/1 waitlist invitations" do
53:     test "resolves a waitlist id and creates the invitation with no profile or Stripe customer" do
54:       created_by_id = insert_principal!("admin@example.com")
55:       waitlist_entry = insert_waitlist_entry!("ada@example.com")
56: 
57:       insert_waitlist_profile!(waitlist_entry.id,
58:         first_name: "Ada",
59:         last_name: "Lovelace",
60:         phone_number: "+353810000001",
61:         date_of_birth: ~D[1990-01-01]
62:       )
63: 
64:       args = %{
65:         "invites" => [waitlist_entry.id],
66:         "user" => %{"id" => created_by_id, "email" => "admin@example.com"}
67:       }
68: 
69:       # Subscribe to the admin's Notification realtime topic before perform so
70:       # the commit-safe broadcast attempt is observable. The bulk invitation
71:       # workflow must produce exactly one notification_created signal for the
72:       # admin alongside its existing processing Notification row.
73:       Phoenix.PubSub.subscribe(Dhc.PubSub, Broadcaster.topic(created_by_id))
74: 
75:       assert :ok = BulkInviteWorker.perform(%Oban.Job{args: args})
76: 
77:       assert %Invitation{} = invitation = Repo.get_by(Invitation, email: "ada@example.com")
78:       assert invitation.status == "pending"
79:       assert invitation.waitlist_id == waitlist_entry.id
80:       assert invitation.created_by_principal_id == created_by_id
81:       assert invitation.date_of_birth == ~D[1990-01-01]
82:       assert invitation.first_name == "Ada"
83:       assert invitation.last_name == "Lovelace"
84:       assert invitation.phone_number == "+353810000001"

86:       # ALE-162: the prospective Principal id is a fresh UUID.

103:
